```{r}
#| label: load-libraries
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(scales)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(showtext)

# Keep in step with `dpi:` in the YAML header above. If they disagree, showtext
# sizes every glyph against the wrong resolution and all text scales wrongly.
REPORT_DPI <- 300
REF_WIDTH  <- 10
BASE_SIZE  <- 12

font_add_google("Source Sans 3", "Source Sans 3")
showtext_auto()
# showtext sizes glyphs against its own dpi setting, not the device's. Left at the
# 96 dpi default while the device renders higher, every axis label, strip and
# legend entry comes out proportionally too small across the whole report.
showtext_opts(dpi = REPORT_DPI)

base_theme <- theme(
  strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = "black"),
  plot.background = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = BASE_SIZE) + base_theme)

# Apparent text size in the rendered HTML is base_size / fig-width, because Quarto
# scales every figure to the same container width. A 16-inch figure is downscaled
# twice as hard as an 8-inch one, so with a fixed base_size its labels land at half
# the size. Scaling base_size with the width keeps text constant across figures.
theme_width <- function(w) {
  theme_bw(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = BASE_SIZE * w / REF_WIDTH) +
    base_theme
}

update_geom_defaults("text",  list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 11 / .pt))
update_geom_defaults("label", list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 11 / .pt))

# --- Shared log axes ---------------------------------------------------------
# Every log-scaled axis in this report goes through these, so tick labels read
# 1,000 rather than a mixture of 1,000 and 1e+03. scales::breaks_log() replaces
# trans_breaks(), which is deprecated from scales 1.3.0.
#
# expand_top adds headroom above the highest bar. Set it wherever count labels
# are drawn on top of bars, otherwise the topmost label is clipped by the panel
# edge.

scale_y_log10_std <- function(expand_top = FALSE, ...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = if (expand_top) expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)) else waiver(),
    ...
  )
}

scale_x_log10_std <- function(...) {
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    ...
  )
}

# Exon counts are small integers, so the default log breaks (1, 3, 10, 30) read
# oddly for a number of exons. Force integer breaks instead. The axis stays
# logarithmic because the distribution is heavily skewed towards 1-2 exons.
scale_y_log10_exons <- function(...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
    labels = scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1),
    ...
  )
}

# --- Palette -----------------------------------------------------------------
# One discrete palette for the whole report. ggplot2's default hue palette is
# not colourblind-safe and sat next to viridis and Brewer fills in other panels,
# so the same biotype could appear in three different colours. viridis is
# colourblind-safe and prints legibly in greyscale.

options(
  ggplot2.discrete.fill = function(...) scale_fill_viridis_d(..., option = "D", end = 0.92),
  ggplot2.discrete.colour = function(...) scale_colour_viridis_d(..., option = "D", end = 0.92)
)

# --- Chromosome ordering -----------------------------------------------------
# Facet chromosomes in genomic order (1, 2, ... 10, 11 ... X, Y, MT) rather than
# the alphabetical order a plain sort() gives, which would interleave 10 and 11
# between 1 and 2.
#
# The optional chr prefix is stripped before the numeric test. Ensembl names
# contigs "1" while GENCODE names them "chr1"; without stripping, no GENCODE
# name matches the numeric pattern and every chromosome falls through to the
# alphabetical branch.

order_chromosomes <- function(x) {
  values <- unique(as.character(x))
  bare <- sub("^chr", "", values, ignore.case = TRUE)

  is_numeric_chr <- grepl("^[0-9]+$", bare)
  numeric_sorted <- values[is_numeric_chr][order(as.numeric(bare[is_numeric_chr]))]
  other_sorted <- sort(values[!is_numeric_chr])

  # droplevels so a chromosome absent from the data never reserves an empty panel
  droplevels(factor(x, levels = c(numeric_sorted, other_sorted)))
}

# --- Chromosome distribution figures -----------------------------------------
# Ensembl and GENCODE both mix hundreds of unplaced contigs (GL000195.1,
# KI270728.1) in with the real chromosomes. On a GENCODE v50 run, 47 of 72
# seqnames were scaffolds carrying 1-12 transcripts each. Pattern rather than a
# fixed list: the pipeline runs on any Ensembl/GENCODE organism, so this also has
# to cover roman-numeral (yeast I-XVI), arm-suffixed (fly 2L/3R) and organelle
# names.
is_assembled_chromosome <- function(x) {
  bare <- toupper(sub("^chr", "", as.character(x), ignore.case = TRUE))
  grepl("^([0-9]{1,2}[A-Z]?|[IVXL]{1,6}|[XYZW]|M|MT|MITO|MTDNA|PT|PLTD)$", bare)
}

# Width follows the number of chromosomes on the x axis, height the number of
# biotype rows. One row per biotype rather than one panel, so a genome-wide figure
# is a single grid instead of five stacked panels sharing an axis.
chr_dist_layout <- function(n_x, n_rows, x_w = 0.34, row_h = 0.42,
                            min_w = 7, max_w = 16, min_h = 3, max_h = 12) {
  w_want <- n_x * x_w + 2.4
  if (w_want > max_w) {
    warning(sprintf("chr_dist_layout: %d x categories want %.1f in, capped at %.1f; labels may collide.",
                    n_x, w_want, max_w))
  }
  list(width  = min(max_w, max(min_w, w_want)),
       height = min(max_h, max(min_h, n_rows * row_h + 2.0)))
}

# --- Count grids -------------------------------------------------------------
# Counts across two categorical axes, drawn as a heatmap with the value printed in
# each cell.
#
# This replaced a family of log10 lollipop grids, for a reason the data made
# plain: some cells are genuinely zero -- chr13 has no novel protein-coding calls
# on the ONT run -- and log10 has no zero, so those points were simply absent from
# the figure. An absent lollipop reads identically to a category that was never in
# the data. Bars would have the mirror-image problem: a log axis gives a bar no
# honest baseline, which is why lollipops were used in the first place.
#
# A heatmap has neither problem. Colour carries the order of magnitude
# perceptually, the printed number carries the exact value including zero, and
# there is no baseline to be arbitrary about. Three of the plots this replaced
# already printed the count as text, so the lollipop was carrying no information
# the number did not.
#
# `df` needs one row per cell with a count column. Missing combinations are
# completed to zero rather than dropped -- that is the point of the change.
plot_count_heatmap <- function(df, x, y, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                               x_lab = NULL, y_lab = NULL, facet = NULL,
                               legend_name = "Transcripts", angle_x = 90) {

  # The facet variable is completed too, otherwise a combination present in one
  # panel and absent from another leaves a gap in the second -- the same silent
  # omission the log axis used to cause.
  full <- if (is.null(facet)) {
    tidyr::complete(df, {{ x }}, {{ y }}, fill = list(count = 0))
  } else {
    tidyr::complete(df, {{ x }}, {{ y }}, .data[[facet]], fill = list(count = 0))
  }
  cap <- max(full$count, 1)

  p <- ggplot(full, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = forcats::fct_rev(as.factor({{ y }})))) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = ifelse(count > 0, count, NA_real_)),
              colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = format(count, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
                  # White ink only on the dark end of the ramp. The threshold is
                  # on the log scale, because that is what the fill is mapped on.
                  colour = count > 0 & log10(pmax(count, 1)) > 0.62 * log10(cap)),
              size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"),
                        na.value = "grey55", guide = "none") +
    # Log-transformed fill: counts span orders of magnitude, and a linear ramp
    # would render everything except the largest cell as the same pale tile.
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "log10",
                         na.value = NA, labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ","),
                         name = legend_name) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme(
      panel.grid        = element_blank(),
      panel.border      = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = angle_x,
                                       hjust = if (angle_x == 0) 0.5 else 1,
                                       vjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position   = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(1.1, "cm"),
      legend.key.width  = unit(0.35, "cm"),
      strip.text        = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title        = element_text(size = rel(1.33), face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = rel(1.08), hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = x_lab, y = y_lab)

  if (!is.null(facet)) p <- p + facet_grid(cols = vars(.data[[facet]]),
                                           scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")
  p
}

# Chromosomes along x, biotypes down y. Expects columns: chromosome, biotype, count.
#
# fig_width is taken here rather than appended by the caller: theme_width() returns
# a *complete* theme, and a complete theme replaces everything set before it. Added
# after the fact it would silently wipe the heatmap's panel, axis and legend
# settings, leaving gridlines and ticks over the tiles.
plot_chr_distribution <- function(df, title, subtitle, fig_width = 10) {
  base <- plot_count_heatmap(df, x = chromosome, y = biotype,
                             title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
                             x_lab = "Chromosome", y_lab = NULL)

  base +
    theme_width(fig_width) +
    theme(
      panel.grid        = element_blank(),
      panel.border      = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y      = element_blank(),
      legend.position   = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(1.1, "cm"),
      legend.key.width  = unit(0.35, "cm"),
      plot.title        = element_text(size = rel(1.33), face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = rel(1.08), hjust = 0.5)
    )
}

# --- UpSet ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hand-rolled rather than pulled from ComplexUpset, which is not in the container.
# Two aligned ggplots: intersection sizes on top, membership matrix below.
#
# Sets must be attributes an item can hold *simultaneously*. Mutually exclusive
# categories -- biotype, class code, chromosome -- are not sets: every
# non-singleton intersection would be empty by construction and the matrix would
# be dead space. Those belong in `fill_col` instead, which stacks each bar.
#
# `df` needs one row per item, a logical column per entry in `sets`, and
# optionally `fill_col` naming a categorical column.
plot_upset <- function(df, sets, fill_col = NULL, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                       max_intersections = 12, empty_label = "no flags") {

  present <- sets[vapply(sets, function(s) s %in% names(df), logical(1))]
  if (!length(present) || !nrow(df)) return(NULL)

  mat <- as.data.frame(lapply(df[present], function(x) !is.na(x) & x))
  names(mat) <- present

  # The signature is the set of memberships, so identical combinations collapse.
  sig <- apply(mat, 1, function(r) paste(present[r], collapse = " & "))
  sig[!nzchar(sig)] <- empty_label

  counted <- data.frame(sig = sig, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  counted$fill <- if (!is.null(fill_col) && fill_col %in% names(df)) {
    as.character(df[[fill_col]])
  } else {
    "all"
  }

  totals <- sort(table(counted$sig), decreasing = TRUE)
  keep   <- names(totals)[seq_len(min(max_intersections, length(totals)))]

  bars <- counted[counted$sig %in% keep, , drop = FALSE] %>%
    dplyr::count(sig, fill, name = "n")
  bars$sig <- factor(bars$sig, levels = keep)

  set_sizes <- vapply(present, function(s) sum(mat[[s]]), integer(1))
  set_lab   <- sprintf("%s  (%s)", present, format(set_sizes, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

  # Matrix: one dot per (intersection, set). Filled where the set is a member.
  grid_df <- expand.grid(sig = keep, set = present, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  grid_df$member <- mapply(function(s, k) {
    k != empty_label && s %in% strsplit(k, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  }, grid_df$set, grid_df$sig)
  grid_df$sig   <- factor(grid_df$sig, levels = keep)
  grid_df$set_f <- factor(set_lab[match(grid_df$set, present)], levels = rev(set_lab))

  # The connecting segment spans the members of each intersection, which is what
  # makes a combination readable at a glance rather than dot by dot.
  spans <- grid_df[grid_df$member, ] %>%
    dplyr::group_by(sig) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(lo = min(as.integer(set_f)), hi = max(as.integer(set_f)),
                     .groups = "drop")

  n_fill <- length(unique(bars$fill))

  p_bar <- ggplot(bars, aes(x = sig, y = n, fill = fill)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.62) +
    geom_text(data = dplyr::summarise(dplyr::group_by(bars, sig),
                                      n = sum(n), .groups = "drop"),
              aes(x = sig, y = n, label = format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.35, size = 2.9) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)),
                       labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    { if (n_fill > 1) scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9, name = NULL)
      else scale_fill_manual(values = "#3B6FB6", guide = "none") } +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x     = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x     = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      legend.position  = if (n_fill > 1) "top" else "none",
      plot.title       = element_text(size = rel(1.33), face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = rel(1.08), hjust = 0.5),
      plot.margin      = margin(5.5, 5.5, 0, 5.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, y = "Transcripts")

  p_mat <- ggplot(grid_df, aes(x = sig, y = set_f)) +
    geom_segment(data = spans, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 aes(x = sig, xend = sig, y = lo, yend = hi),
                 colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = member), size = 2.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey15", `FALSE` = "grey85"),
                        guide = "none") +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.title         = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks         = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = margin(0, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5)
    )

  cowplot::plot_grid(p_bar, p_mat, ncol = 1, align = "v", axis = "lr",
                     rel_heights = c(1, 0.16 + 0.09 * length(present)))
}
```

## Introduction

This report provides a detailed analysis of a transcriptome assembled from long-read RNA sequencing data. The primary goal is to identify and characterize both known (annotated) and novel protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts. These results are organized into three main sections:

1.  **Overall Assembly Statistics:** A high-level view of the assembly results.
2.  **Annotated RNAs Overview:** Characteristics of known transcripts identified in your samples.
3.  **Novel RNAs Overview:** An exploration of the newly discovered protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts.

This automated report was generated by the `integrativebioinformatics/pulposeq` pipeline.

### Metadatasets curation

Downstream to the assembly with **Bambu** [^1], the raw extended annotations and count matrices from `BambuOutput` were curated and subset to generate a final subset of genes and transcripts that are relevant for downstream analyses. The main curation process involved the following steps:

[^1]: Chen, Ying, et al. "Context-aware transcript quantification from long-read RNA-seq data with Bambu." Nature methods 20.8 (2023): 1187-1195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01908-w

1.  Any gene or transcript that had zero counts across all samples were subset out(check the subset quantification files in the results folder `bambu_subset/`).
2.  Novel transcript isoforms were submitted to coding potential prediction with **RNAmining** [^2] and were compared to the reference annotations by **GffCompare** [^3], and classified as protein-coding or lncRNA among distinct sub-biotypes.
3.  The structure of the isoforms is characterized, and metadata regarding isoform-level structure is retrieved directly from the reference annotation and assembly GTF files with **rtracklayer**[^4].
4.  Finally, annotations, count matrices and characterization metadata are standardized into comprehensive metadatasets that are easily accessible for downstream analyses, and the overall statistics of the assembly are summarized in the following sections of this report.

[^2]: Ramos, Thaís AR, et al. "RNAmining: A machine learning stand-alone and web server tool for RNA coding potential prediction." F1000Research 10 (2021): 323. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.52350.2

[^3]: Pertea, Geo, and Mihaela Pertea. "GFF utilities: GffRead and GffCompare." F1000Research 9 (2020): ISCB-Comm. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.23297.1

[^4]: Lawrence, Michael, Robert Gentleman, and Vincent Carey. "rtracklayer: an R package for interfacing with genome browsers." Bioinformatics 25.14 (2009): 1841-1842. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp328

Final validated results are organized into the folders `bambu_validated`, `novel_trancripts` and `annotated_transcripts` in the output directory.

::: callout-note
Any transcripts **NOT** matching the following criteria were filtered out:

- Length ≥ 200bp

- Classified as intergenic (`u`), intronic (`i`), antisense (`x`), multi-exonic matching at least 1 reference splice junction (`j`) or intron retained (`m` for all introns and `n` for partial number of introns) by GffCompare (`class_codes`).

- Assembled according to a known strand direction (+/-).
:::

::: details
### pulposeq follows the current consensus statement for lncRNA classification

Transcriptional complexity poses challenges for the accurate classification of lncRNAs, which are often intergenic, intronic, antisense and/or alternatively spliced transcripts from genes of other distinct biotypes (e.g. protein-coding genes, pseudogenes, etc). Relying solely on the parent locus biotype may oversimplify important aspects of the nature and structure of **any RNA molecule**.

pulposeq adresses this conceptual bottleneck when classifying novel isoforms that overlap functionally distinct loci by implementing a dual-layer classification strategy. Novel isoforms transcribed from previously annotated loci are assigned with individual transcript biotypes that were resolved independently based on:

1.  Coding potential predictions;
2.  Structural features identified based on their length, relationship with reference transcripts and their exon-intron structures.

Consequently, a newly discovered isoform lacking coding potential but originating from a known protein-coding locus or any other gene biotype is classified strictly as a novel lncRNA transcript. This standardization process follows the current recommendations of the consensus statement of Mattick and colleagues [^5] for lncRNA classification and naming.

#### Why the report says *candidate*

A transcript labelled a **novel lncRNA candidate** satisfies five conditions: it is absent from the reference annotation, at least 200 nt long, assembled on a declared strand, carries an accepted gffcompare class code, and is predicted non-coding. That is a well-defined set, and it is the set this report counts.

It is not a set of validated lncRNAs. A coding-potential prediction is evidence about composition, not about whether a transcript is an independent transcriptional unit, and for some class codes it says less than it appears to. The [Structural Validation of Novel Calls](#structural-validation-of-novel-calls) section reports what other evidence each candidate carries. Two class codes are handled separately for exactly this reason:

- `m` and `n` (**intron retention**) are routed to their own category rather than sorted by coding potential, because a retained intron is non-coding sequence and therefore determines that prediction in advance.
- `i` (**intronic**) transcripts on the host gene's strand are sequence-identical to part of that host's pre-mRNA, so position alone cannot distinguish an independent transcript from a fragment of the host. These are flagged, never dropped.

Nothing is filtered on this basis. A candidate set with the evidence stated per member is a stronger result than an unqualified count.
:::

[^5]: Mattick, J.S., Amaral, P.P., Carninci, P. et al. Long non-coding RNAs: definitions, functions, challenges and recommendations. Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 24, 430–447 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41580-022-00566-8

## Overall Assembly Statistics

This section presents a quantitative isoform-level overview of the transcriptome assembly. Based on the curated subsets from Bambu, we gathered all metadata of genes and transcripts that were detected and quantified. We categorize these into three groups:

- **Total:** All unique features identified.
- **Annotated:** Features that match an existing reference annotation (e.g., Ensembl). These have IDs starting with `ENS`.
- **Novel:** Features newly discovered by Bambu that are not in the reference annotation. These have IDs starting with `Bambu`.

::: callout-warning
Bambu Read Classes (RCs) that are not compatible with any transcript are classified as incompatible and not considered for isoform-level quantification, but all incompatible RCs are still assignable to genes, and Bambu uses them for gene quantification by default. In order to generate a final curated and relevant subset of gene counts, only genes transcribing compatible and effectively quantified isoforms are kept after the validation process.
:::

```{r}
#| label: run-metrics
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

metrics <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$bambu_metrics, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
vsum    <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$validation_summary, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)

get_metric <- function(k) {
  if (is.null(metrics)) return(NA_character_)
  v <- metrics$value[metrics$metric == k]
  if (length(v)) as.character(v[1]) else NA_character_
}

cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
cat("## Run parameters and validation yield\n\n")

ndr <- get_metric("ndr_used")
cat(sprintf("**Novel discovery rate (NDR):** %s%s\n\n",
            ifelse(is.na(ndr), "not recorded", ndr),
            if (identical(get_metric("ndr_requested"), "auto"))
              " — selected automatically by Bambu" else " — set explicitly"))

if (!is.null(vsum)) {
  cat(knitr::kable(
    data.frame(
      Feature      = vsum$feature_type,
      Retained     = format(vsum$retained, big.mark = ","),
      Total        = format(vsum$total, big.mark = ","),
      `Retained %` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * vsum$fraction_retained),
      check.names  = FALSE
    ), format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
}
cat("\n:::\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: get-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# List bambu outputs to account for assembled and quantified genes/transcripts
bambu_outputs <- c(
  genes = params$counts_genes,
  transcripts = params$counts_transcript,
  fullLength = params$fl_counts_transcript,
  uniquelyMapped = params$u_counts_transcript
)

# Check if files exist
files_exist <- sapply(bambu_outputs, file.exists)
if (!all(files_exist)) {
  missing_files <- bambu_outputs[!files_exist]
  stop("Error: The following files were not found: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

# Store results in a list
results_list <- list()
for (name in names(bambu_outputs)) {
  current_file <- bambu_outputs[[name]]
  tryCatch({
    data <- read.delim(current_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
    id_column <- data[[1]]
    total_count <- nrow(data)
    annotated_count <- sum(startsWith(id_column, "ENS"))
    novel_count <- sum(startsWith(id_column, "Bambu"))
    file_result <- data.frame(Bambu = name, Total = total_count, Annotated = annotated_count, Novel = novel_count)
    results_list[[name]] <- file_result
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Warning: Could not process file '", basename(current_file), "' (named '", name, "'). Skipping.\n", sep = "")
    cat("Error message:", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

# Organize results
if (length(results_list) > 0) {
  bambu_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  rownames(bambu_df) <- NULL
  bambu_df <- bambu_df %>%
    mutate(FeatureType = if_else(Bambu == "genes", "Gene", "Transcript")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")
  write.csv(bambu_df, "Bambu_assembly_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed from the provided list.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-to-plot-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

if (!exists("bambu_df")) {
  stop("Error: The data frame 'bambu_df' was not found.")
}
custom_labels <- c("genes" = "Genes", "transcripts" = "All transcripts", "fullLength" = "Full length", "uniquelyMapped" = "Uniquely mapped")
bambu_df$Status <- factor(bambu_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
bambu_df$Bambu <- factor(bambu_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("genes", "transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-gene-transcript-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Summary of Assembled Genes and Transcripts.** This figure displays the total counts of genes (A) and various categories of transcripts (B) identified by Bambu. Counts are broken down into 'Total', 'Annotated' (known), and 'Novel' (newly discovered). Transcript counts are further detailed for all transcripts, only full-length and uniquely mapped transcripts."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

bambu_gene_data <- bambu_df %>% filter(FeatureType == "Gene")
bambu_gene_plot <- ggplot(bambu_gene_data, aes(x = Status, y = Count, fill = Status)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(title = "Genes", x = "\nStatus", y = "No. of genes\n") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

bambu_transcript_data <- bambu_df %>% filter(FeatureType == "Transcript")
bambu_transcript_data$Bambu <- factor(bambu_transcript_data$Bambu, levels = names(custom_labels)[-1])
levels(bambu_transcript_data$Bambu) <- custom_labels[-1]

bambu_transcript_plot <- ggplot(bambu_transcript_data, aes(x = Bambu, y = Count, fill = Status)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.3) +
  labs(title = "Transcripts", x = "\nAssembly", y = "No. of transcripts\n", fill = "Status") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "right")

bambu_plot <- plot_grid(bambu_gene_plot, bambu_transcript_plot, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(0.7, 1.3), labels = "AUTO", label_y = 0.85)
bambu_plot
```

#### Long non-coding RNAs vs protein-coding RNAs

```{r}
#| label: get-lnc-pc-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# --- 1A. Check if Annotated Transcriptome Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The annotated transcriptome metadata file was not found at: ", params$transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 1B. Check if Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The novel transcript metadata file was not found at: ", params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 2A. Import Annotated Transcriptome Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  ann_txome <- read.csv(params$transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading annotated transcriptome metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# --- 2B. Import Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  novel_tx <- read.csv(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading novel transcript metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# Display biotype comes from the category the transcript was routed into, not from
# the coding prediction. The two agree for u/i/x/j, where the prediction is real
# information. They must not be conflated for m and n: a retained intron is
# non-coding sequence, so the prediction there restates the structure rather than
# adding to it, and reading it back off `prediction` would put those transcripts
# among the lncRNA candidates after the classification deliberately took them out.
NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(
  novel_lncRNA          = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  novel_protein_coding  = "novel protein_coding",
  novel_retained_intron = "novel retained intron"
)

if ("transcript_biotype" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
  novel_tx$biotype <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS[novel_tx$transcript_biotype])
  novel_tx$biotype[is.na(novel_tx$biotype)] <- "novel (unclassified)"
} else {
  # Metadata written before the intron-retention split carries no biotype column.
  novel_tx$biotype <- ifelse(novel_tx$prediction == "coding",
                             "novel protein_coding", "novel lncRNA candidate")
}

is_retained <- novel_tx$biotype == "novel retained intron"

# Separate the raw transcript IDs first
raw_nov_pc_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$prediction == "coding"    & !is_retained])
raw_nov_lnc_tx <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$prediction == "non-coding" & !is_retained])
raw_nov_ir_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[is_retained])

# --- 3. Read Bambu IDs from the output files ---
bambu_ids <- list()
for (name in names(bambu_outputs)) {
  if (name == "genes") next # Skip genes file for this section
  current_file <- bambu_outputs[[name]]
    # Only read the first column (IDs)
    data_ids <- read.delim(current_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")[[1]]
    bambu_ids[[name]] <- as.character(data_ids)
}

# Identify if annotated transcript IDs contain versioning suffix
if (any(grepl("\\.", bambu_ids$transcripts))) {
  version_suffix <- TRUE
} else {
  version_suffix <- FALSE
}

# --- 4. Extract ID vectors for each category (Transcripts Only) ---
ids <- list(
  # Protein-coding
  ann_pc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  },
  
  # lncRNAs
  ann_lnc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  },

  # Filter to only include true novel protein-coding features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_pc_tx = raw_nov_pc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_pc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Filter to only include true novel lncRNA features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_lnc_tx = raw_nov_lnc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_lnc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Intron-retention events are a third category, not a subset of either of the
  # above -- omitting them here would drop them from every summary below.
  nov_ir_tx = raw_nov_ir_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_ir_tx, "Bambu")]
)

# Helper function to count overlaps between Bambu outputs and our target IDs
count_overlap <- function(bambu_set, target_ids) {
  if (is.null(bambu_set) || length(bambu_set) == 0) return(0)
  sum(bambu_set %in% target_ids)
}

# --- 5. Quantify across categories ---
results_biotype <- list()

BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(pc = "Protein-coding", lnc = "lncRNA", ir = "Intron retention")

for (bt in names(BIOTYPE_LABELS)) {
  biotype_label <- unname(BIOTYPE_LABELS[bt])

  # Transcript Level (Check all three transcript files)
  for (tx_cat in c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")) {
    # Intron retention exists only as a novel category -- there is no annotated
    # counterpart to look up, so ann_pc/ann_lnc have no ann_ir sibling.
    ann_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("ann_", bt, "_tx")]])
    nov_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("nov_", bt, "_tx")]])
    tot_t <- ann_t + nov_t
    
    results_biotype[[paste0(bt, "_", tx_cat)]] <- data.frame(
      FeatureType = "Transcript", Biotype = biotype_label, Bambu = tx_cat,
      Total = tot_t, Annotated = ann_t, Novel = nov_t
    )
  }
}

# --- 6. Organize and Save Results ---
if (length(results_biotype) > 0) {
  biotype_df <- do.call(rbind, results_biotype) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")

  # Ensure proper factor ordering
  biotype_df$Status <- factor(biotype_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
  biotype_df$Bambu <- factor(biotype_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))

  write.csv(biotype_df, "Bambu_lncRNA_PC_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed to build the biotype summary.\n")
}
```

Bambu reports each transcript in three matrices: all assigned reads, reads spanning the transcript's full structure, and reads mapping to it uniquely. The three are **nested** — full-length and unique support are both subsets of total — so the informative question is not how many transcripts appear in each, but which transcripts appear in *both*.

A transcript with full-length **and** unique support is evidenced directly. One with neither was quantified entirely from expectation-maximisation over reads that never spanned it, and is the weakest thing in the assembly.

```{r}
#| label: support-sets-prep
#| include: false

# One row per detected transcript, with membership of the two support matrices as
# logical columns. Membership, not counts: this figure answers "which transcripts
# have which kinds of evidence", and the count distributions come later.
support_category <- c(
  ann_pc_tx  = "annotated protein-coding",
  ann_lnc_tx = "annotated lncRNA",
  nov_pc_tx  = "novel protein-coding",
  nov_lnc_tx = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  nov_ir_tx  = "novel retained intron"
)

detected <- unique(bambu_ids$transcripts)

cat_of <- rep(NA_character_, length(detected))
for (k in names(support_category)) {
  hit <- is.na(cat_of) & detected %in% ids[[k]]
  cat_of[hit] <- support_category[[k]]
}

support_sets <- data.frame(
  transcript_id            = detected,
  category                 = cat_of,
  `full-length support`    = detected %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
  `unique support`         = detected %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped,
  check.names              = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors         = FALSE
)

# Transcripts in the counts matrix that belong to none of the five categories are
# biotypes this figure does not track (small RNAs, pseudogenes and so on). Kept,
# and named, rather than silently dropped.
support_sets$category[is.na(support_sets$category)] <- "other biotypes"
support_sets$category <- factor(
  support_sets$category,
  levels = c("annotated protein-coding", "annotated lncRNA", "other biotypes",
             "novel protein-coding", "novel lncRNA candidate", "novel retained intron")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-lnc-pc-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Read support for every transcript in the validated assembly.** Each bar is a distinct combination of evidence, with the dot matrix below showing which kinds of support that combination has. Bars are stacked by transcript category. The rightmost bar — neither full-length nor unique support — is quantified purely from expectation-maximisation. Set sizes are given in the row labels."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5

plot_upset(
  support_sets,
  sets      = c("full-length support", "unique support"),
  fill_col  = "category",
  title     = "Which transcripts have which kinds of read support",
  subtitle  = "Full-length and unique support are both subsets of total, so no transcript can have either without being detected",
  empty_label = "neither"
)
```

## Sample-level Expression Overview

Bambu produces a PCA and expression heatmaps summarising how samples relate to one another. The figures below are shown twice: once for the **raw assembly**, exactly as Bambu produced it, and once after the transcriptome has been **validated and curated** by the metadata refinement steps. The raw assembly still contains novel transcript calls that were later discarded, so differences between the two views show how much those discarded calls were influencing the sample-level signal.

```{r}
#| label: plot-availability
#| include: false

plot_params <- list(
  raw_pca                 = params$raw_pca,
  raw_pca_grouped         = params$raw_pca_grouped,
  raw_heatmap_gene        = params$raw_heatmap_gene,
  raw_heatmap_transcript  = params$raw_heatmap_transcript,
  post_pca                = params$post_pca,
  post_pca_grouped        = params$post_pca_grouped,
  post_heatmap_gene       = params$post_heatmap_gene,
  post_heatmap_transcript = params$post_heatmap_transcript
)

# A plot is only embedded if the file is present and non-empty, so a stub run or
# a partially completed execution does not break the render.
plot_available <- vapply(plot_params, function(p) {
  !is.null(p) && file.exists(p) && file.info(p)$size > 0
}, logical(1))

# include_graphics must be handed a vector: called inside a loop it would not be
# auto-printed and nothing would be embedded.
show_plots <- function(keys) {
  paths <- unlist(plot_params[keys][plot_available[keys]], use.names = FALSE)
  if (length(paths) > 0) knitr::include_graphics(paths) else NULL
}
```

## Annotated RNAs Overview

In this section, we focus exclusively on the **annotated** portion of the transcriptome. These are transcripts that match known entries in public databases. By analyzing their biotypes, lengths, and exon structures, we can understand the composition of the known transcriptome in our samples and establish a baseline for comparison with novel transcripts.

### Biotype Distribution Analysis

Biotypes classify RNAs based on their function or characteristics (e.g., `protein_coding`, `lncRNA`, `miRNA`).

```{r}
#| label: data-prep-annotated
#| include: false

# Load and prepare data
summary_data <- ann_txome %>% 
  group_by(gene_biotype, transcript_biotype) %>% 
  summarise(count = n_distinct(ensembl_transcript_id_version), .groups = 'drop')

# Categorize biotypes
protein_coding <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding")
lncRNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "lncRNA")
pseudogene_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene")) %>% mutate(category = "Pseudogene")
small_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA"))
Tcell_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("TR_V_gene", "TR_J_gene", "TR_D_gene", "TR_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "TCR elements")
IG_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("IG_V_gene", "IG_J_gene", "IG_D_gene", "IG_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "Immunoglobulin elements")

# Gather all biotypes that have already been classified above
classified_biotypes <- unique(c(
  protein_coding$gene_biotype,
  lncRNAs$gene_biotype,
  pseudogene_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  small_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  Tcell_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  IG_RNAs$gene_biotype
))

# Dynamically filter for ANY biotype that isn't in the classified list
other_RNAs_explicit <- summary_data %>% 
  filter(!gene_biotype %in% classified_biotypes) %>% 
  mutate(category = "all other biotypes")

# Group all other RNAs for the aggregated plot
all_other_RNAs <- bind_rows(pseudogene_RNAs, Tcell_RNAs, IG_RNAs, other_RNAs_explicit) %>% 
  group_by(category) %>% 
  summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = 'drop')

all_other_RNAs$category <- factor(all_other_RNAs$category, levels = c("Pseudogene", "TCR elements", "Immunoglobulin elements", "all other biotypes"))

# Plotting function.
#
# Transcript biotypes across the columns, the gene biotype they belong to as the
# row, count printed in each cell. `row` and `col` keep the argument order the
# lollipop version used, so the call sites below are unchanged apart from p4.
create_plot <- function(data, row, col, title, fig_width = 16) {
  plot_count_heatmap(data, x = {{ col }}, y = {{ row }},
                     title = title,
                     x_lab = "Transcript biotypes", y_lab = "Gene biotype",
                     legend_name = "Transcripts") +
    # Base size scaled to the width these panels are actually drawn at, and applied
    # here rather than at the call site: adding a complete theme replaces everything
    # set before it, so appending it later would wipe the tweaks below.
    theme_width(fig_width) +
    theme(
      panel.grid       = element_blank(),
      panel.border     = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      legend.position  = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(0.9, "cm"),
      legend.key.width  = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      plot.title       = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y     = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x     = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.margin      = margin(0.4, 1, 0.4, 1, "cm")
    )
}

# Generate plots. The x-axis labels are kept on every panel: they name the
# transcript biotypes, which differ between panels and are the point of the
# figure. Under the lollipop layout x was the gene biotype, identical down every
# panel, which is why it used to be blanked.
p1 <- create_plot(protein_coding, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "Protein-coding RNAs")
p2 <- create_plot(lncRNAs, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "LncRNAs")
p3 <- create_plot(small_RNAs, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "Small RNAs")
# x and fill were the same column here, which as a grid would draw a diagonal.
# A constant row turns it into the single strip the data actually is.
p4 <- create_plot(mutate(all_other_RNAs, group = "all other"), group, category, "All Other RNAs")
p5 <- create_plot(pseudogene_RNAs, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "Pseudogene RNA diversity")
p6 <- create_plot(other_RNAs_explicit, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "Other RNAs (detailed)")
p7 <- create_plot(Tcell_RNAs, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "TCR element RNAs")
p8 <- create_plot(IG_RNAs, gene_biotype, transcript_biotype, "Immunoglobulin element RNAs")
```

#### Overview of Major RNA Categories

The plots below summarize the counts of transcripts grouped into four major categories. Counts span several orders of magnitude, so colour is mapped on a log10 scale while the exact number is printed in each cell.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 10

panel1 <- plot_grid(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1.3, 1), labels = "AUTO", label_y = 0.85)
panel1
```

#### Other RNA categories

This panel provides a more detailed breakdown of the diverse and less common RNA biotypes, including pseudogenes and elements related to the immune system.

```{r}
#| label: fig-panel-2
#| fig-cap: "**Detailed Breakdown of Other RNA Categories.** This figure provides a closer look at specific RNA families: (A) diversity within Pseudogene RNAs, (B) T-cell receptor (TCR) elements, (C) Immunoglobulin (IG) elements, and (D) other variety of RNA types."
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 10

top_row_panel2 <- plot_grid(p5, ncol = 1, labels = "A", label_y = 0.85)
bottom_row_panel2 <- plot_grid(p7, p8, p6, ncol = 3, labels = c("B", "C", "D"), label_y = 0.85)
panel2 <- plot_grid(top_row_panel2, bottom_row_panel2, nrow = 2, rel_heights = c(1, 1))
panel2
```
:::

#### Gene Biotype Diversity Across Chromosomes

This visualization maps the distribution of different gene biotypes across all chromosomes, revealing genomic hotspots for certain types of genes.

> The layout of this figure adapts to how many chromosomes your data covers, so it should not need manual adjustment. If you do want to change the proportions, the per-panel allowance is set by `facet_layout()` in the `load-libraries` chunk; the plot itself is `fig-gb-across-chr`.

```{r}
#| label: prep-chr-data
#| include: false

chr_gb <- ann_txome %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene"), "pseudogene", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(gene_biotype %in% c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA"), "small_RNA", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(!gene_biotype %in% c("pseudogene", "small_RNA", "protein_coding", "lncRNA"), "other", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(chr_class = if_else(is_assembled_chromosome(chromosome_name), "assembled", "scaffold")) %>%
  group_by(chr_class, chromosome = chromosome_name, biotype = gene_biotype) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# droplevels so a biotype absent from the data never reserves an empty panel row
chr_gb$biotype <- droplevels(factor(chr_gb$biotype,
  levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "small_RNA", "pseudogene", "other")))

chr_gb_asm <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "assembled") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = order_chromosomes(chromosome))
chr_gb_scf <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "scaffold") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

chr_asm_lay <- chr_dist_layout(nlevels(chr_gb_asm$chromosome), nlevels(chr_gb_asm$biotype))
chr_scf_lay <- chr_dist_layout(nlevels(chr_gb_scf$chromosome), nlevels(chr_gb_scf$biotype))
has_scaffolds <- nrow(chr_gb_scf) > 0
```

::: panel-tabset
##### Assembled chromosomes

```{r}
#| label: fig-gb-across-chr
#| fig-cap: "**Chromosomal Distribution of Gene Biotypes.** Transcript isoforms of each biotype annotated on every assembled chromosome. Colour carries the order of magnitude, the printed number the exact count -- including the zeros a log axis cannot show."
#| fig-width: !expr chr_asm_lay$width
#| fig-height: !expr chr_asm_lay$height

plot_chr_distribution(
  chr_gb_asm,
  "Gene Biotype Diversity Across Chromosomes",
  "Transcript isoforms per biotype on each assembled chromosome",
  fig_width = chr_asm_lay$width
)
```

##### Unplaced scaffolds

```{r}
#| label: fig-gb-across-scaffolds
#| fig-cap: "**Gene Biotypes on Unplaced Scaffolds.** The same breakdown for contigs not assigned to an assembled chromosome. These typically carry a handful of transcripts each."
#| fig-width: !expr chr_scf_lay$width
#| fig-height: !expr chr_scf_lay$height
#| eval: !expr has_scaffolds

plot_chr_distribution(
  chr_gb_scf,
  "Gene Biotype Diversity Across Unplaced Scaffolds",
  sprintf("%d unplaced contigs carrying annotated transcripts",
          nlevels(chr_gb_scf$chromosome))
,
  fig_width = chr_scf_lay$width
)
```
:::

### Transcript Length Analysis

Here, we investigate the length of transcripts across different biotypes.

```{r}
#| label: prep-tx-length-data

selected_tx <- ann_txome %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
selected_tx$gene_biotype <- factor(selected_tx$gene_biotype, levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
median_stx <- selected_tx %>% group_by(gene_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')
median_pc <- selected_tx %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding") %>% group_by(transcript_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length_txb = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')
median_lnc <- selected_tx %>% filter(gene_biotype == "lncRNA") %>% group_by(transcript_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length_txb = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')

p10 <- ggplot(selected_tx, aes(x = gene_biotype, y = transcript_length, fill = factor(gene_biotype))) +
  geom_boxplot() + labs(title = "Transcript length across gene biotypes", x = "Gene biotype", y = "Transcript length (log10 scale)", fill = "Gene biotype\n(median length)") +
  scale_y_log10_std() + scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.92, labels = paste0(median_stx$gene_biotype, " (", round(median_stx$median_length, 2), ")"))

p11 <- selected_tx %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding") %>%

p12 <- selected_tx %>% filter(gene_biotype == "lncRNA") %>%
```

## Novel Protein-Coding and lncRNA Candidates Overview

This section focuses on the characterization of newly identified protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts that were not present in the reference annotation. Every count below is a count of **candidates**: transcripts that meet the classification criteria and have not yet been shown to be independent transcriptional units. The evidence gathered for them is reported in [Structural Validation of Novel Calls](#structural-validation-of-novel-calls).

> **About the Tools:**
>
> - **GFFRead:** This tool is used to transform the GTF annotation of the novel transcripts into a FASTA file based on a reference annotation.
> - **GFFCompare:** This tool is used to compare the assembled novel transcripts (from Bambu) against a reference annotation file. It classifies each novel transcript based on its relationship to known transcripts (e.g., a novel isoform of a known gene, a transcript in an intergenic region, etc).
> - **RNAmining:** This tool analyzes the sequence of novel transcripts to predict whether they are likely to be protein-coding or non-coding (like lncRNAs).

### Biotype and Classification of Novel Transcripts

```{r}
#| label: load-data-novel
#| include: false

class_counts <- novel_tx %>% group_by(biotype, classification) %>% summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "**GFFCompare Classification of Novel Transcripts.** This bar chart shows the counts of novel protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts according to their GFFCompare classification code."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

p20 <- plot_count_heatmap(
  class_counts, x = classification, y = biotype,
  title = "GFFCompare classification of novel protein-coding and lncRNA candidates",
  x_lab = "Classification", y_lab = "Category", angle_x = 45
)
p20
```

```{r}

chr_tb_novel <- novel_tx %>%
  mutate(chr_class = if_else(is_assembled_chromosome(seqnames), "assembled", "scaffold")) %>%

  mutate(chromosome = order_chromosomes(chromosome))
chr_novel_scf <- chr_tb_novel %>% filter(chr_class == "scaffold") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

                                     nlevels(chr_novel_asm$biotype))
```

## Structural Validation of Novel Calls

Novel transcripts are candidates, not findings. This section reports the
structural evidence gathered for each one, and nothing here filters the output:
every transcript counted above is still present. The point is to say which
candidates carry warning signs and which do not, so that a count is never quoted
without knowing what sits behind it.

Two tests run over the alignments, both asking structural questions that need no
threshold tuned to a particular genome:

- **Strand versus host.** A transcript inside a host gene's intron, on the
  *opposite* strand, cannot be explained by that host's pre-mRNA. On the *same*
  strand it can, and position alone cannot tell the two apart.
- **Boundary read-through and host junctions.** A discrete transcript has reads
  that end where it ends. Reads running past its boundaries, or carrying splice
  junctions belonging to the host rather than to the candidate, came from a
  longer molecule.

```{r}
#| label: context-prep
#| echo: false

read_csv_safe <- function(path) {
  if (is.null(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  df <- tryCatch(read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) NULL else df
}

ctx_flags   <- read_csv_safe(params$context_flags)
ctx_summary <- read_csv_safe(params$context_summary)
novel_ir    <- read_csv_safe(params$novel_intron_retention_meta)

ctx_metric <- function(key) {
  if (is.null(ctx_summary)) return(NA_integer_)
  v <- ctx_summary$value[ctx_summary$metric == key]
  if (length(v)) as.integer(v[1]) else NA_integer_
}

fmt_n <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "not recorded" else format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

```{r}
#| label: context-callout
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(ctx_flags)) {
  cat('::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Structural validation did not run\n\n")
  cat("No `novel_context_flags.csv` was available, so the candidates in this report ")
  cat("carry no structural evidence. Every count above should be read as unvalidated.\n")
  cat(":::\n")
} else {
  same  <- ctx_metric("same_strand_as_host")
  opp   <- ctx_metric("opposite_strand_to_host")
  isame <- ctx_metric("intronic_same_strand")
  ijunc <- ctx_metric("intronic_same_strand_with_host_junction")
  none  <- ctx_metric("no_reads_recovered")

  cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Structural evidence, in short\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** candidates evaluated.\n", fmt_n(ctx_metric("candidates_evaluated"))))
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** lie within a host gene: %s on the same strand, %s on the opposite strand.\n",
              fmt_n(ctx_metric("with_host_gene")), fmt_n(same), fmt_n(opp)))
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** are intronic *and* on the host's strand, which is the ambiguous population.\n",
              fmt_n(isame)))
  cat(sprintf("- Of those, **%s** are supported by reads carrying one of the host's splice junctions, which is evidence those reads came from the host.\n",
              fmt_n(ijunc)))
  if (!is.na(none) && none > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("- **%s** recovered no overlapping reads at all and cannot be assessed either way.\n",
                fmt_n(none)))
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

### Strand relative to the host gene

```{r}
#| label: fig-context-strand
#| fig-cap: "**Strand of each novel transcript relative to its host gene, by class code.** Opposite-strand transcripts are unambiguous: the host's pre-mRNA cannot produce them. Same-strand intronic transcripts are the population that needs the read-level evidence below. Transcripts with no host gene are intergenic and have nothing to compare against."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| eval: !expr !is.null(ctx_flags)

strand_df <- ctx_flags %>%
  mutate(relation = case_when(
    is.na(same_strand_as_host) ~ "no host gene",
    same_strand_as_host        ~ "same strand as host",
    TRUE                       ~ "opposite strand to host"
  )) %>%
  count(class_code, relation, name = "count")

ggplot(strand_df, aes(x = class_code, y = count, fill = relation)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "same strand as host"     = "#D95F02",
    "opposite strand to host" = "#1B9E77",
    "no host gene"            = "grey70"
  )) +
  scale_y_log10_std(expand_top = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Novel transcript strand relative to the host gene",
       subtitle = "Same-strand intronic transcripts cannot be separated from host pre-mRNA by position alone",
       x = "gffcompare class code", y = "Transcripts (log10 scale)", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Read-level evidence

```{r}
#| label: fig-context-reads
#| fig-cap: "**Fraction of supporting reads that run past a transcript's boundaries, and fraction carrying one of the host gene's splice junctions.** A discrete transcript sits near zero on both. Values near one mean the reads supporting the call belong to a longer molecule, most likely the host's unspliced pre-mRNA. Only transcripts with a host gene and at least one recovered read are shown."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| eval: !expr !is.null(ctx_flags)

reads_df <- ctx_flags %>%
  filter(!is.na(same_strand_as_host), reads_total > 0) %>%
  select(class_code, frac_crossing_boundary, frac_with_host_junction) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(frac_crossing_boundary, frac_with_host_junction),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    frac_crossing_boundary  = "reads crossing a boundary",
    frac_with_host_junction = "reads carrying a host junction"))

ggplot(reads_df, aes(x = class_code, y = fraction, fill = measure)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", begin = 0.25, end = 0.75) +
  labs(title = "Read-level evidence against each novel transcript",
       subtitle = "Higher is worse: the supporting reads do not stop where the transcript does",
       x = "gffcompare class code", y = "Fraction of supporting reads", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Which warning signs occur together

The figures above each show one signal at a time. What decides whether a candidate
is worth distrusting is whether the signals **agree** — and that is a question
about combinations, not about any single distribution.

Each bar below is one exact combination of flags. The transcripts to look at first
are in the bar carrying the most flags at once: intronic, on the host's strand,
unspliced, supported by reads that run past its boundaries and carry the host's
junctions. That is the profile of a pre-mRNA fragment, and it is one bar you can
point at rather than a conjunction you have to assemble from five figures.

Every flag here is structural and threshold-free — each is a count being zero or
non-zero, not a value crossing a cutoff.

```{r}
#| label: evidence-sets-prep
#| include: false

evidence_sets <- NULL

if (!is.null(ctx_flags)) {
  ev <- ctx_flags
  if (exists("novel_tx") && "exon" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
    ev <- dplyr::left_join(ev, novel_tx[, c("qry_id", "exon")], by = "qry_id")
  } else {
    ev$exon <- NA_character_
  }

  # Full-length support is membership of Bambu's fullLengthCounts matrix, which is
  # a zero/non-zero fact rather than a threshold on a fraction.
  fl_ids <- if (exists("bambu_ids") && !is.null(bambu_ids$fullLength)) {
    bambu_ids$fullLength
  } else {
    character(0)
  }

  evidence_sets <- ev %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      `mono-exonic`                 = !is.na(exon) & exon == "mono-exonic",
      `same strand as host`         = same_strand_as_host %in% TRUE,
      `reads cross a boundary`      = reads_crossing_boundary > 0,
      `reads carry a host junction` = reads_with_host_junction > 0,
      `no full-length support`      = !(qry_id %in% fl_ids),
      class_code                    = factor(class_code)
    )

  if (!nrow(evidence_sets)) evidence_sets <- NULL
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-evidence-upset
#| fig-cap: "**Combinations of structural warning signs across novel transcript candidates.** Each bar is one exact combination; the dot matrix below names it. Bars are stacked by gffcompare class code, which is a mutually exclusive attribute and therefore a fill rather than a set. Set sizes are in the row labels. A candidate appearing in the leftmost bar carries no warning signs at all."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| eval: !expr !is.null(evidence_sets)

plot_upset(
  evidence_sets,
  sets = c("mono-exonic", "same strand as host", "reads cross a boundary",
           "reads carry a host junction", "no full-length support"),
  fill_col = "class_code",
  title    = "Structural warning signs, by combination",
  subtitle = "More flags at once means less of the evidence is explained by the candidate being a real, discrete transcript",
  empty_label = "no warning signs"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: evidence-upset-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (!is.null(evidence_sets)) {
  n_all <- sum(evidence_sets$`same strand as host` &
               evidence_sets$`reads cross a boundary` &
               evidence_sets$`reads carry a host junction`, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_clean <- sum(!evidence_sets$`same strand as host` &
                 !evidence_sets$`reads cross a boundary` &
                 !evidence_sets$`reads carry a host junction`, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "Of %s candidates, **%s** carry all three host-relationship flags at once ",
    "(same strand, boundary read-through, host junctions), and **%s** carry none ",
    "of them. Neither number is a verdict: the first is the set to inspect, the ",
    "second is the set with nothing arguing against it.\n"),
    format(nrow(evidence_sets), big.mark = ","),
    format(n_all, big.mark = ","),
    format(n_clean, big.mark = ",")))
}
```


### Full-length and uniquely-mapped support

Bambu reports, per transcript, how many reads support it in total, how many span
its full structure, and how many map to it uniquely. Read alongside the class
code, these separate a transcript that reads *fit* from one that reads merely
*overlap*.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Read the low tail, not the high one

A novel model was built from the very reads then counted against it, so a high
full-length fraction is partly circular and is not confirmation of anything. The
informative direction is the **low** tail: a candidate whose supporting reads
mostly fail to span it is a fragment of something longer. Treat this as a screen
that points at transcripts worth inspecting, not as a verdict on any of them.
:::

```{r}
#| label: support-prep
#| echo: false

# Per-transcript totals across all samples. The first column is the transcript id
# and every numeric column after it is one sample.
read_support <- function(path, label) {
  df <- tryCatch(read.delim(path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(NULL)
  num <- df[, vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  if (!ncol(num)) return(NULL)
  out <- data.frame(transcript_id = as.character(df[[1]]),
                    value = rowSums(num, na.rm = TRUE),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(out)[2] <- label
  out
}

sup_total <- read_support(params$counts_transcript,    "reads_total")
sup_full  <- read_support(params$fl_counts_transcript, "reads_full_length")
sup_uniq  <- read_support(params$u_counts_transcript,  "reads_unique")

support <- NULL
if (!is.null(sup_total) && !is.null(sup_full) && !is.null(sup_uniq)) {
  support <- sup_total %>%
    inner_join(sup_full, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(sup_uniq, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(novel_tx[, c("qry_id", "class_code", "biotype", "exon")],
               by = c("transcript_id" = "qry_id")) %>%
    filter(reads_total > 0) %>%
    mutate(full_length_fraction = reads_full_length / reads_total,
           unique_fraction      = reads_unique      / reads_total)
  if (!nrow(support)) support <- NULL
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-support-fraction
#| fig-cap: "**Full-length and uniquely-mapped read support for novel transcripts, by class code and exon structure.** Each panel is one support measure. Low full-length support means the reads behind a call do not span it; low unique support means those reads are compatible with other transcripts too, so the count came largely from expectation-maximisation rather than from unambiguous evidence."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7
#| eval: !expr !is.null(support)

support_long <- support %>%
  select(class_code, exon, full_length_fraction, unique_fraction) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(full_length_fraction, unique_fraction),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    full_length_fraction = "full-length / total",
    unique_fraction      = "uniquely mapped / total"))

ggplot(support_long, aes(x = class_code, y = fraction, fill = exon)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Read support for novel transcripts",
       subtitle = "Low values mark candidates whose supporting reads fit them poorly",
       x = "gffcompare class code", y = "Fraction of supporting reads",
       fill = "Exon class") +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  theme_width(12)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-support-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Median read support by novel transcript category and class code."
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr !is.null(support)

support %>%
  group_by(biotype, class_code) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `median full-length` = sprintf("%.2f", median(full_length_fraction)),
            `median unique`      = sprintf("%.2f", median(unique_fraction)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(biotype, class_code) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "markdown")
```

### Intron retention as its own category

```{r}
#| label: intron-retention-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(novel_ir)) {
  cat("No intron-retention events were found in this run.\n")
} else {
  n_m <- sum(novel_ir$class_code == "m")
  n_n <- sum(novel_ir$class_code == "n")
  hosts <- sort(table(novel_ir$host_gene_biotype, useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE)
  host_names <- names(hosts)
  host_names[is.na(host_names)] <- "no host gene"
  host_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", host_names, as.integer(hosts)), collapse = ", ")

  cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Why these are reported separately\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("This run produced **%d** intron-retention transcripts: %d with every reference intron accounted for (`m`) and %d that additionally fail to cover the full reference structure (`n`).\n\n",
              nrow(novel_ir), n_m, n_n))
  cat("They are **not** sorted by coding potential. RNAmining scores length-normalised trinucleotide composition, and retained intronic sequence has never been under coding selection, so it pulls the composition toward non-coding in proportion to how much of the transcript it makes up. Filing these as lncRNA candidates on that basis would restate their structure rather than add evidence. The prediction is kept as a column in `novel_intron_retention_metadata.csv`; it is simply not used to route them.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("Host gene biotypes here: %s. This matters, because a retained-intron transcript of a lncRNA gene and one of a protein-coding gene are different findings, and hosts are frequently not protein-coding.\n",
              host_txt))
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

## Genomic Context

Coverage and transcript models drawn together at selected loci. The bigWig tracks
behind these figures are published alongside the report, so any region can be
opened in IGV to explore beyond the windows chosen here.

```{r}
#| label: genomic-context-prep
#| echo: false

gc_clean   <- read_csv_safe(params$genomic_context_candidates)
gc_flagged <- read_csv_safe(params$intronic_context_candidates)

# A figure is embedded only when its PNG was actually staged, so a stub run or a
# partially failed draw leaves a gap rather than a broken image.
embed_figures <- function(df, file_col, tab_col, caption_fn) {
  if (is.null(df) || !(file_col %in% names(df)) || !(tab_col %in% names(df))) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  present <- df[!is.na(df[[file_col]]) & file.exists(df[[file_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(present)) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(present))) {
    cat(sprintf("## %s\n\n", present[[tab_col]][i]))
    cat(sprintf("![%s](%s)\n\n", caption_fn(present[i, ]), present[[file_col]][i]))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

### Known genes carrying novel isoforms

Each panel shows the gene's full exonic footprint, then every isoform at the
locus with novel ones highlighted, then one coverage track per sample on a shared
scale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-clean
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_clean, "figure", "label", function(r) {
  sprintf("%s at %s:%s-%s. %d isoforms, %d novel.",
          r$label, r$chrom, format(r$win_s, big.mark = ","),
          format(r$win_e, big.mark = ","), r$n_tx, r$n_novel)
})
```

### Flagged intronic candidates

These are chosen for the opposite reason: each is an intronic candidate on its
host's strand whose supporting reads run past its boundaries or carry the host's
splice junctions. They are drawn windowed on the **whole host intron**, because a
window drawn tightly around a truncated fragment looks like a discrete transcript
whatever it is. The flanking intron is where the difference shows.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## What to look for

A candidate that really is host pre-mRNA shows coverage running flat across the
entire intron and continuous with the flanking exons. A candidate that is a
genuine independent transcript shows a discrete block of coverage with quiet
intron either side. If a flagged candidate looks discrete here, the flag is what
needs revisiting, not the transcript.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-flagged
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_flagged, "figure", "qry_id", function(r) {
  sprintf("%s inside an intron of %s (%s). %d reads: %d cross a boundary, %d carry a host junction.",
          r$qry_id,
          ifelse(is.na(r$host_gene_name) | !nzchar(r$host_gene_name),
                 r$host_gene_id, r$host_gene_name),
          r$host_gene_biotype, r$reads_total,
          r$reads_crossing_boundary, r$reads_with_host_junction)
})
```
